name: The Science of Coffee
description: Questions covering: Botany, Chemistry, Roasting, Extraction, Brewing, Sensory Science, Processing...

questions.question: Which botanical species accounts for the majority of global specialty coffee production?
questions.explanation_correct: Coffea arabica is the most widely cultivated species for high-quality specialty coffee.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Coffea canephora and Coffea liberica are other cultivated species; specialty quality is not determined by species alone. Excelsa is often classified within C. liberica.

questions.question: In many coffee-growing regions, what weather change following a dry period can trigger flowering?
questions.explanation_correct: Rain after a dry period can synchronize coffee flowering; the timing and response depend on species and local conditions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Soil, wind and light conditions affect the plant, but rain following a dry spell is a common flowering trigger.

questions.question: Which secondary metabolite serves as the primary methylxanthine alkaloid in coffee beans?
questions.explanation_correct: Caffeine is the most prevalent alkaloid found in coffee beans responsible for their stimulating effects.
questions.explanation_incorrect: While theophylline and theobromine are also methylxanthines, they exist in significantly smaller concentrations in raw coffee.

questions.question: Which major group of phenolic compounds contributes antioxidant activity to coffee?
questions.explanation_correct: Chlorogenic acids are the major group of polyphenols found in coffee that provide significant antioxidant activity.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Citric acid is an organic acid, while amino acids are protein building blocks; carboxylic acids are a broad chemical category. Other substances can also contribute antioxidant activity.

questions.question: Which chemical transformation occurring during heat application creates the complex flavor compounds and brown pigments in coffee?
questions.explanation_correct: The Maillard reaction is a chemical reaction between amino acids and reducing sugars that gives browned food its distinctive flavor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Caramelization involves heat-driven reactions of sugars, whereas the Maillard reaction involves reducing sugars and amino compounds such as free amino acids.

questions.question: What term describes heat-driven decomposition of organic material under little or no oxygen?
questions.explanation_correct: Pyrolysis is thermal decomposition under limited or absent oxygen. Roasting involves several overlapping reactions and is not necessarily oxygen-free.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Condensation, sublimation and evaporation are different processes.

questions.question: What substance is primarily used as the solvent for extracting soluble solids from roasted coffee ground material?
questions.explanation_correct: Water is the solvent commonly used to brew coffee; it dissolves many, but not all, compounds in roasted beans.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Ethanol, oil and acetone are not the standard solvent used to prepare brewed coffee.

questions.question: Which brewing device steeps coffee grounds in hot water before separating them with a plunger?
questions.explanation_correct: A French press steeps grounds in water, then uses a mesh plunger to separate most solids.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A siphon also involves immersion, while V60 and Chemex are commonly used for percolation; they do not use the French press plunger.

questions.question: Which of the primary gustatory sensations is most commonly associated with roasted coffee solids?
questions.explanation_correct: Bitterness is a primary taste sensation chemically triggered in coffee by various compounds like caffeine and chlorogenic acid lactones.
questions.explanation_incorrect: While coffee can exhibit acidity, bitterness is a fundamental, dominant sensory attribute of the roasted bean itself.

questions.question: Which acid found in coffee is also strongly associated with the tart taste of citrus fruit?
questions.explanation_correct: Citric acid occurs in coffee and citrus fruits. Perceived acidity in coffee depends on several acids and brewing conditions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Malic, acetic and tartaric acids also occur in foods and can contribute different sensory impressions.

questions.question: What term describes coffee fermentation carried out in a controlled low-oxygen environment?
questions.explanation_correct: Anaerobic fermentation refers to fermentation under oxygen-limited conditions; processing setups and residual oxygen vary.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Washed, natural and honey describe broader processing methods and may be combined with different fermentation conditions.

questions.question: What is the biological species associated with the genetic lineage of Robusta coffee?
questions.explanation_correct: Coffea canephora is the botanical species that constitutes the classification of Robusta coffee.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other listed species bear different botanical classifications and commercial profiles.

questions.question: Which organic acid is a primary product of the breakdown of chlorogenic acids during the roasting of coffee?
questions.explanation_correct: Quinic acid is formed when chlorogenic acids undergo hydrolysis and subsequent decomposition during the roast.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Other acids may be produced or altered through processing and roasting; quinic acid is associated with breakdown of chlorogenic acids.

questions.question: Which unit is commonly used to report the size of individual ground-coffee particles?
questions.explanation_correct: Particle sizes are often reported in micrometres, also called microns; a distribution includes the amounts of particles at different sizes.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Other units could be converted mathematically, but micrometres are convenient for these small particles.

questions.question: Which brewing machine typically uses a pump to force hot water through a compacted bed of coffee under pressure?
questions.explanation_correct: Many espresso machines use pumps, often targeting around 9 bar at the coffee bed; some espresso machines use levers instead.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A moka pot uses vapor pressure; a French press and Chemex do not use a mechanical espresso pump.

questions.question: Which gas forms much of the bubbles in espresso crema?
questions.explanation_correct: Carbon dioxide released from roasted coffee forms much of the crema gas phase; proteins, polysaccharides and lipids also influence foam properties.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Air and water vapor may also occur in crema, but carbon dioxide is the coffee-derived gas identified here.

questions.question: Which coffee cultivar originated as a natural genetic mutation of the Bourbon variety?
questions.explanation_correct: Caturra is a well-known dwarf mutation found in the Bourbon variety of coffee.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Typica and Gesha are distinct varieties, while Maragogype is known for its large bean size mutation.

questions.question: Which insect pest is considered the most significant threat to the global production of coffee cherries?
questions.explanation_correct: The coffee berry borer is a highly destructive beetle that burrows directly into the coffee fruit.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Leaf miners and mealybugs are pests, but they do not cause the same level of direct economic loss as the berry borer.

questions.question: What disease caused by the fungus Hemileia vastatrix produces rust-colored lesions on coffee leaves?
questions.explanation_correct: Coffee leaf rust is caused by Hemileia vastatrix and can damage leaves and crop yields.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other named diseases have different causes or symptoms; Cercospora can also affect leaves.

questions.question: What gas is released in large quantities during the de-gassing phase that immediately follows the roasting of coffee?
questions.explanation_correct: Carbon dioxide is produced by chemical reactions in the roasting process and is trapped in the bean structure prior to release.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Carbon dioxide is the dominant gas released from roasted coffee; the other choices do not describe the main degassing product.

questions.question: Which taste is commonly associated with an underextracted coffee brew?
questions.explanation_correct: Underextracted coffee can taste sour or sharp when extraction is insufficient; taste also depends on the beans, roast and recipe.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bitterness may become more prominent with extensive extraction, but taste alone does not prove the extraction level.

questions.question: What common negative sensory descriptor is characteristic of an overextracted coffee cup?
questions.explanation_correct: Overextracted coffee may taste bitter or feel drying and astringent. The sensation depends on many extracted compounds and brewing conditions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Acidic, fruity and floral notes are not the drying mouthfeel described; no one descriptor alone proves overextraction.

questions.question: Which coffee variety is recognized as a natural hybrid between Coffea arabica and Coffea canephora?
questions.explanation_correct: Hibrido de Timor is a spontaneous cross that emerged in the mid-20th century, combining the hardiness of Robusta with the quality of Arabica.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bourbon, Geisha, and SL28 are specific cultivars of the Coffea arabica species.

questions.question: Which processing method dries depulped coffee with some or all mucilage remaining on the parchment?
questions.explanation_correct: In honey processing, coffee is depulped and dried with some or all mucilage attached; the term overlaps with pulped natural.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Fully washed coffee has its mucilage removed before drying; natural processing dries intact fruit, and wet-hulling removes parchment while the beans are still damp.

questions.question: What green pigment in coffee leaves absorbs light for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation_correct: Chlorophyll absorbs light used in photosynthesis. Green coffee seeds have a different tissue composition and their color should not be attributed to this pigment alone.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Carotenoids and anthocyanins are other plant pigments, while tannins are a group of phenolic compounds.

questions.question: What is the device used to hold the ground coffee in an espresso machine called?
questions.explanation_correct: A portafilter is the handle-mounted basket mechanism used in espresso machines to hold the coffee bed.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The tamper is used to compress the grounds, while the doser and dispenser move grounds, but do not hold them during percolation.

questions.question: What is the main storage tissue that makes up most of a coffee bean?
questions.explanation_correct: The endosperm is the main storage tissue in a coffee seed and forms most of the roastable bean.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Epidermis, cortex and cambium are other plant tissues, not the main storage tissue of a coffee seed.

questions.question: What is the name of the outermost layer or skin of the coffee cherry?
questions.explanation_correct: The exocarp is the protective outer layer or skin of the coffee fruit.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other terms refer to the internal pulpy layer, the protective parchment, or the entire fruit wall as a whole.

questions.question: Which layer of the coffee cherry resides between the outer skin and the inner parchment?
questions.explanation_correct: The mesocarp, or pulp, is the fleshy middle layer of the coffee cherry containing mucilage.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The exocarp is the skin, and the endocarp is the internal parchment layer.

questions.question: What corresponds to the parchment layer that directly encases the coffee seed?
questions.explanation_correct: The endocarp is the hardened layer known as parchment that surrounds the seed.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The exocarp is the skin, and the mesocarp is the juicy pulp.

questions.question: What is the common coffee-industry name for the thin seed coat that often becomes chaff during roasting?
questions.explanation_correct: Silverskin is the thin seed coat, also called the testa or spermoderm; fragments can separate as chaff during roasting.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Parchment is the endocarp, while pulp and mucilage are fruit layers outside it.

questions.question: Which class of volatile organic compounds contributes significantly to the fruity aroma of coffee?
questions.explanation_correct: Esters are volatile compounds generally responsible for the aromatic properties related to fruity and floral notes in coffee.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Other volatile classes, including some aldehydes and terpenes, can also contribute fruit or floral impressions; aromas depend on specific molecules and their concentrations.

questions.question: What compound is primarily responsible for the distinctive earthy or 'soil-like' aroma in some coffee profiles?
questions.explanation_correct: Geosmin is a common earth-smelling compound produced by certain bacteria and often detected in earthy coffees.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other compounds relate to roasted profiles, sulfurous notes, or chemical byproducts, not specifically earthy-soil scents.

questions.question: Which term describes the genome state of the Arabica coffee species?
questions.explanation_correct: Arabica is a natural hybrid possessing four sets of chromosomes, making it a tetraploid species.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Most other coffee species, including Robusta, are diploid.

questions.question: Which brewer heats water into an upper chamber, then draws brewed coffee through a filter as the lower chamber cools?
questions.explanation_correct: In a siphon brewer, expanding vapor pushes water upward; after heating stops, cooling lowers pressure and draws the brewed coffee back through a filter.
questions.explanation_incorrect: French press, pour-over and AeroPress use different mechanisms to separate grounds from liquid.

questions.question: Which pressure unit is commonly used on espresso machine gauges and specifications?
questions.explanation_correct: Espresso pressure is commonly expressed in bar; a machine can also report pressure in other equivalent units.
questions.explanation_incorrect: PSI, atmospheres and torr are also pressure units, though bar is commonly used in espresso specifications.

questions.question: What piece of equipment is specifically designed with a thin, curved spout for precise water flow control during manual brewing?
questions.explanation_correct: The gooseneck kettle allows baristas to control the speed and location of the water pour accurately.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Standard kettles have wider spouts that do not allow for the same level of precise laminar flow.

questions.question: Which two organizations collaborated on the 2016 Coffee Taster’s Flavor Wheel?
options: Specialty Coffee Association and World Coffee Research
questions.answer: Specialty Coffee Association and World Coffee Research
questions.explanation_correct: The Specialty Coffee Association updated its flavor wheel in 2016 in collaboration with World Coffee Research, drawing on the WCR Sensory Lexicon.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other pairs were not the collaboration responsible for that 2016 update.

questions.question: Which solvent has become widely used in decaffeination because it is naturally found in fruit?
questions.explanation_correct: Ethyl acetate occurs naturally in fruit and is also manufactured for use as a decaffeination solvent.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Methylene chloride is another decaffeination solvent; carbon dioxide and water are used in other processes. Dichloromethane is another name for methylene chloride.

questions.question: Which decaffeination solvent can be used above its critical temperature and pressure, where it has both gas-like and liquid-like properties?
questions.explanation_correct: Supercritical carbon dioxide can act as a solvent for caffeine extraction under controlled temperature and pressure.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options do not name the carbon dioxide process used for decaffeination.

questions.question: What is the common term for the global tropical region where coffee plants are cultivated between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn?
questions.explanation_correct: The Bean Belt describes the equatorial region providing the ideal climate for coffee growth.
questions.explanation_incorrect: These alternative terms describe geographic or meteorological zones but are not the industry-standard term for coffee cultivation regions.

questions.question: What physical property is commonly measured as mass per unit volume when evaluating green coffee beans?
questions.explanation_correct: Bean density is mass per unit volume. Growing conditions, variety and processing can all affect it.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Porosity, solubility and oiliness describe other properties rather than mass per unit volume.

questions.question: Which acid is especially associated with the tart flavor of grapes and is also found in some coffees?
questions.explanation_correct: Tartaric acid occurs in grapes and can occur in coffee. A wine-like impression depends on multiple compounds, not one acid alone.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Citric and acetic acids can also affect coffee flavor; phosphoric acid is inorganic.

questions.question: Which ecological outcome can diverse shade-grown coffee systems support compared with full-sun monocultures?
questions.explanation_correct: Shade trees and varied vegetation can provide habitat for more species, although outcomes depend on management and local conditions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Higher yield and pest sterility are not universal consequences of shade; biodiversity describes the ecological benefit.

questions.question: What term defines the mass ratio of dry coffee grounds to the total weight of water used during the extraction process?
questions.explanation_correct: A brew ratio compares the mass of dry grounds with the mass of brewing water. Final strength also depends on extraction and retained water.
questions.explanation_incorrect: TDS describes dissolved concentration, while extraction yield estimates the fraction of grounds dissolved.

questions.question: What is the name of the foam that can form on top of an espresso?
questions.explanation_correct: Crema is a foam containing gas bubbles dispersed in coffee liquid; oils, proteins and polysaccharides affect its properties.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mousse, flavone and colloid are not the standard name for the foam on espresso. Crema alone does not prove the shot was properly extracted.

questions.question: Which hydrophobic compounds play a crucial role in creating the mouthfeel and aroma retention of espresso?
questions.explanation_correct: Coffee lipids, or oils, are vital emulsified components that provide the heavy, smooth texture typically attributed to espresso.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Proteins and polysaccharides influence texture differently, but lipids are the primary hydrophobic emulsion agents.

questions.question: What is the traditional semi-washed processing method unique to Indonesia that involves removing the parchment while the coffee is still damp?
questions.explanation_correct: Giling Basah, also known as 'wet-hulling,' is a signature Indonesian method resulting in a distinct body and earthiness.
questions.explanation_incorrect: These other processing terms originate from Latin American or African coffee traditions, not the specific Indonesian wet-hulling technique.

questions.question: Which Arabica variety gives its name to a major historical lineage that includes Maragogipe?
questions.explanation_correct: Typica is one of the important historical Arabica lineages; Maragogipe is a natural mutation of Typica. Bourbon is another foundational lineage.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bourbon is a separate important lineage, while Geisha and SL28 have different histories.

questions.question: Which dwarf variety of Arabica was developed in Brazil as a cross between Mundo Novo and Caturra?
questions.explanation_correct: Catuai is a high-yielding, dwarf hybrid specifically bred to be compact for efficient farming.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Other options refer to distinct mutation lineages (such as Caturra or Pacas) rather than the specific Catuai cross.

questions.question: Which mineral ion in water contributes to general hardness and is represented by the symbol Mg²⁺?
questions.explanation_correct: Magnesium contributes to water hardness alongside calcium. Water mineral composition can influence extraction and flavor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Calcium also contributes to hardness, but Mg²⁺ denotes magnesium; sodium and potassium have different symbols.

questions.question: Which chemical compound acts as the primary alkaline buffer in brewing water to prevent sudden changes in acidity during extraction?
questions.explanation_correct: Bicarbonate provides the buffering capacity needed to neutralize excess acids, essentially modulating the perceived acidity of the coffee.
questions.explanation_incorrect: These other ions lack the specific buffering functionality of bicarbonates in the context of coffee brewing water chemistry.

questions.question: To which specific neuro-receptors does caffeine bind to temporarily inhibit the sensation of tiredness?
questions.explanation_correct: Caffeine is an antagonist that binds to adenosine receptors, preventing the neurotransmitter from signaling fatigue to the brain.
questions.explanation_incorrect: These other receptors regulate mood and alertness through different mechanisms not directly targeted by caffeine's primary function.

questions.question: What is the initial phase of the roasting process, characterized by the absorption of energy as moisture evaporates from the seed?
questions.explanation_correct: The drying phase is endothermic because it requires energy input to strip the green coffee of its significant internal water content.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Maillard reactions and first crack are later roasting markers; heat transfer and reactions can overlap throughout roasting.

questions.question: What physics property of the coffee bed determines the ease with which water passes through ground coffee under pressure?
questions.explanation_correct: Permeability refers to the ability of the coffee grounds to allow water flow, which is heavily influenced by grind size and distribution.
questions.explanation_incorrect: These other terms describe fluid dynamics or surface forces, not the specific physical property of the coffee medium bed.

questions.question: In sensory science, what term is used to describe the perceived pleasant acidity that provides life and energy to a cup of coffee?
questions.explanation_correct: Brightness is the industry standard term used to define a lively, pleasant acidity characteristic of high-quality coffee.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Other terms relate to the weight or chemical depth of the flavor, rather than the specific perception of energetic acidity.

questions.question: Which of these names denotes a coffee species rather than an Arabica variety?
questions.explanation_correct: Coffea liberica is a coffee species cultivated commercially in parts of Southeast Asia and West Africa.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Caturra, Bourbon and Typica are Arabica varieties or variety groups. The classification of Excelsa has been debated.

questions.question: What is the common name for the by-product consisting of the dried skin and pulp of the coffee cherry often used for tea?
questions.explanation_correct: Cascara refers to the dried skin and pulp, which is increasingly prepared as a tea-like infusion containing antioxidants.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other terms represent various structures or sublayers of the coffee fruit but do not refer to the edible tea product.

questions.question: What primary chemical process causes the degradation of volatile aromatic compounds in roasted coffee when exposed to air?
questions.explanation_correct: Oxidation contributes to staling in roasted coffee, while loss of volatile compounds also reduces aroma.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other reactions have roles in coffee chemistry, but oxygen exposure and loss of volatiles are major staling mechanisms.

questions.question: Which commercial color scale is commonly used to describe the roast color of coffee?
questions.explanation_correct: Agtron readings estimate roast color using reflectance; instrument setup and sample preparation matter.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Hunter and CIE L*a*b* are also color measurement systems; Brix measures soluble solids rather than coffee roast color.

questions.question: Which analytical instrument is utilized by baristas to measure the concentration of dissolved coffee compounds in a liquid?
questions.explanation_correct: A refractometer measures the refractive index of a liquid to determine the concentration of dissolved solids.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A hygrometer measures humidity and a calorimeter measures heat. Spectrometers can measure concentration in analytical settings, but a coffee refractometer estimates dissolved solids from refractive index.

questions.question: What is the industry term for the percentage of the dry coffee grounds' mass that has been dissolved into the final brew?
questions.explanation_correct: Extraction Yield (or Soluble Yield) measures how much of the original dry coffee weight was dissolved into the water.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) measures the concentration of the liquid, while Brew Ratio is the relationship between dry coffee and water weight.

questions.question: In dry-processed coffee, what mechanical process is employed to remove the dried parchment layer from the green bean?
questions.explanation_correct: Hulling removes dried outer layers; in natural coffee it removes the dried fruit layers and parchment around the beans.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Depulping removes outer fruit before drying in other processes, while polishing and sorting serve different purposes.

questions.question: What is the term for cooling roasted coffee with a controlled spray of water?
questions.explanation_correct: Water quenching is used by some commercial roasters to help stop roasting. Its effect depends on the process and moisture added.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other terms do not specifically name this coffee-roasting cooling technique; water quenching is not universally prohibited.

questions.question: Which specific Arabica cultivar is known for its unusually large bean size resulting from a naturally occurring mutation?
questions.explanation_correct: The Maragogipe cultivar is an elephant-bean variety first discovered in Brazil that is known for its large fruit and leaf structure.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Typica, Geisha, and SL-28 are distinct varieties that do not possess the specific large-bean mutation associated with Maragogipe.

questions.question: Which non-enzymatic browning process involves heat-driven reactions of sugars without requiring amino acids?
questions.explanation_correct: Caramelization involves thermal reactions of sugars, generating color and flavor compounds.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Maillard reactions involve reducing sugars and amino compounds; pyrolysis is a broader term for thermal decomposition under limited oxygen.

questions.question: Which alkaloid compound, abundant in green coffee, serves as a primary precursor for Niacin upon thermal degradation?
questions.explanation_correct: Trigonelline degrades during roasting to form nicotinic acid, also known as Vitamin B3 or Niacin.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Caffeine and theobromine are methylxanthines, and chlorogenic acids are polyphenols that break down into quinic and caffeic acids.

questions.question: What is the sensory property detected by the olfactory receptors during the retronasal sensation of drinking coffee?
questions.explanation_correct: Aroma is perceived both through the nose (orthonasal) and via the back of the throat during the act of drinking (retronasal).
questions.explanation_incorrect: Body, acidity, and mouthfeel are tactile or gustatory perceptions, not olfactory ones.

questions.question: Which descriptor characterizes a coffee grind profile containing two distinct peaks in particle size, typical of burr grinders?
questions.explanation_correct: A bimodal particle-size distribution has two distinct peaks, representing two ranges of particle sizes.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Unimodal means one peak; polymodal can include multiple peaks, including two; Gaussian describes a particular distribution shape.

questions.question: Which decaffeination process uses water, green coffee extract and carbon filtration rather than added organic solvents?
questions.explanation_correct: The Swiss Water Process uses water and green coffee extract, with carbon filtration used to remove caffeine. Water itself acts as a solvent.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Ethyl acetate and methylene chloride are organic solvents, while the supercritical carbon dioxide process uses a different extracting fluid.

questions.question: Which method commonly steeps coffee grounds in cool or room-temperature water for an extended period?
questions.explanation_correct: Immersion cold brew steeps grounds in cool or room-temperature water for an extended period; cold drip is another form of cold extraction.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Japanese-style iced coffee and flash-chilling generally involve hot brewing followed by rapid cooling; cold drip uses slowly passing water rather than immersion.

questions.question: Which East African nation is recognized as the primary historical and genetic center of origin for Coffea arabica?
questions.explanation_correct: Scientific research confirms that Arabica coffee is indigenous to the highland forests of Ethiopia.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania have prominent coffee industries, but the plant is not native to these regions.

questions.question: What is the initial developmental stage of a coffee seed when it begins to sprout and break through its parchment?
questions.explanation_correct: Germination is the process where a seed absorbs water and begins to grow into a seedling.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Flowering, maturation, and fruiting occur much later in the coffee life cycle.

questions.question: Which of these is a yeast genus that can be involved in coffee fermentation?
questions.explanation_correct: Saccharomyces is a yeast genus that can occur or be used as a starter in coffee fermentation. Outcomes depend on strain and conditions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Aspergillus, Penicillium and Rhizopus are genera of filamentous fungi rather than the yeast genus asked for; other yeasts such as Candida can also occur.

questions.question: In professional cupping, which specific term refers to the length and quality of the flavors remaining after the coffee is swallowed or expectorated?
questions.explanation_correct: Aftertaste describes the lingering sensory impression after coffee is swallowed or expectorated; evaluation practices vary by protocol.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Fragrance commonly refers to the smell of dry grounds, while aroma can refer to the smell of wet coffee.

questions.question: Which volatile acid is associated with a vinegar-like smell and can occur in coffee?
questions.explanation_correct: Acetic acid has a vinegar-like smell; its presence or perception can depend on coffee processing and concentration.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Malic, citric and tartaric acids can contribute acidity, but acetic acid is associated with vinegar.

questions.question: What physical parameter is directly accelerated when the surface area of coffee particles is increased through a finer grind?
questions.explanation_correct: Increasing the surface area allows solutes to dissolve more quickly into the water, thereby increasing the extraction rate.
questions.explanation_incorrect: TDS is a result, while vapor pressure and refractive diffusion do not directly describe the speed of solid-liquid mass transfer in this context.

questions.question: What specific accessory, lacking holes, is used during the backflushing procedure to clean an espresso machine's group head?
questions.explanation_correct: A blind filter has no holes, forcing water pressure back through the machine's three-way valve for cleaning.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Portafilter baskets, drip trays, and shower screens are components that do not function as pressure-retaining cleaning tools.

questions.question: What storage change can slow the loss of quality of roasted coffee by slowing many chemical reactions?
questions.explanation_correct: Freezing can slow many staling reactions when coffee is protected from moisture and oxygen, but it does not stop all aging.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Heat, oxygen and light can accelerate deterioration; freezing is not a state of perfect chemical stasis.

questions.question: Which specific color variation of the Bourbon cultivar is celebrated for its distinct, often sweet and bright tasting profile?
questions.explanation_correct: Yellow Bourbon is a naturally occurring sub-variety of the Bourbon plant that exhibits yellow fruit at maturity.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Purple, blue, and black Bourbon are not widely recognized, standard commercial color variants of the Bourbon variety.

questions.question: Which brewing variable changes the thermal energy available for dissolving coffee solubles?
questions.explanation_correct: Water temperature affects extraction rate alongside particle size, contact time and other variables.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Pressure and other factors can also affect extraction; temperature is the thermal variable named here.

questions.question: What is the specialized biological term for the sensory process of identifying coffee aromatics as they pass through the nasal cavity?
questions.explanation_correct: Olfaction is the sensory system responsible for the perception of smells and volatile aromatics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Gustation is taste, somatosensation includes touch, and audition is hearing. Olfaction is one form of chemoreception.

questions.question: Which renowned Ethiopian seed variety is celebrated for its distinctive jasmine-like floral notes?
questions.explanation_correct: Gesha, also spelled Geisha, is an Arabica variety associated with Ethiopia and known for floral cup potential when grown and processed well.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Typica, Bourbon and Caturra are other Arabica varieties; flavor varies with growing conditions and processing.

questions.question: Which compounds, formed during the roasting process from the breakdown of chlorogenic acids, are the primary contributors to the bitterness of coffee?
questions.explanation_correct: Chlorogenic acid lactones contribute to bitterness in roasted coffee; phenylindanes and other compounds also contribute depending on roast.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Trigonelline can also taste bitter and is a precursor of roast compounds; sucrose and lipids have different roles.

questions.question: What primary mechanism of heat transfer is utilized when hot air circulates through a bed of coffee beans in a fluidized-bed roaster?
questions.explanation_correct: Convection involves the transfer of energy through a fluid medium, such as hot air moving through the bean mass.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Conduction involves direct contact with solid surfaces, while radiation relies on electromagnetic wave emission.

questions.question: What primary mechanism of heat transfer occurs during drum roasting when the beans touch the hot metal surface of the roaster wall?
questions.explanation_correct: Conduction occurs when heat energy is transferred via direct contact between particles of matter.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Convection and radiation provide heat via gas circulation or energy waves, respectively, not through physical surface contact.

questions.question: Which specific grinding component represents the physical shearing surfaces that reduce coffee bean size?
questions.explanation_correct: The burrs are the serrated surfaces that crush or cut coffee beans into consistent particle sizes.
questions.explanation_incorrect: An auger feeds the beans, a hopper holds them, and a chute directs the ground particles, but none serve as the primary crushing mechanism.

questions.question: What is the term for the coffee processing method where the fruit is dried intact before de-pulping?
questions.explanation_correct: In natural processing, coffee cherries are dried with the fruit intact before the dried outer layers are removed.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Washed and honey methods remove the outer fruit before drying; wet-hulling removes parchment while beans remain damp.

questions.question: Which coffee processing method removes pulp and mucilage before drying the parchment coffee?
questions.explanation_correct: In washed processing, fruit is depulped and mucilage is removed through fermentation and washing, mechanical demucilaging, or a combination.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Natural processing dries intact fruit; carbonic maceration is a fermentation approach rather than the same complete processing method.

questions.question: Which aromatic compound is a key contributor to the characteristic floral attributes found in high-grade coffee cultivars?
questions.explanation_correct: Linalool is a terpene alcohol that possesses a distinct floral aroma, often associated with high-altitude varieties.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Pyrazine compounds are associated with nutty or toasted notes, while vanillin relates to sweet or spicy aromatic profiles.

questions.question: Which commercial brewing device utilizes proprietary heavy-gauge paper filters to clarify coffee by removing oils and sediment?
questions.explanation_correct: The Chemex employs thick, bonded paper filters designed to extract a clean cup by minimizing coffee solids.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Hario, Melitta and Kalita produce other coffee brewers and paper filters; filtration depends on the filter and brewing method used.

questions.question: What sensory descriptor is used to define the tactile mouthfeel or weight of a coffee when consumed?
questions.explanation_correct: Body relates to the viscosity and tactile sensation of the beverage, often described as light, medium, or heavy.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Finish refers to the lingering aftertaste, acidity refers to flavor brightness, and balance refers to the harmony of all traits.

questions.question: Which sugar is abundant in green coffee and participates in chemical transformations during roasting?
questions.explanation_correct: Sucrose is abundant in green Arabica coffee and breaks down during roasting, contributing to reactions that form aroma and flavor compounds.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Glucose, fructose and mannose can occur in coffee, but sucrose is a prominent sugar in green Arabica beans; perceived sweetness is not explained by sucrose alone.

questions.question: Which specific species of Coffea is known for being botanically autogamous, meaning it is self-pollinating?
questions.explanation_correct: Coffea arabica is largely self-pollinating, although cross-pollination can also occur.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Coffea canephora is mostly cross-pollinating; Liberica and Excelsa also differ from predominantly self-pollinating Arabica.

questions.question: Which plant macronutrient has the chemical symbol N and is important for coffee plant growth?
questions.explanation_correct: Nitrogen is an essential plant macronutrient involved in proteins and chlorophyll production.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Calcium, magnesium and sulfur are also macronutrients, but their symbols are Ca, Mg and S.

questions.question: What is the first audible cracking event during coffee roasting commonly called?
questions.explanation_correct: First crack is associated with pressure buildup and changes in the bean structure, producing audible pops.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Second crack occurs later in some roasting profiles; Maillard reactions and caramelization are chemical processes rather than the first audible crack.

questions.question: What is the time between the start of first crack and the end of roasting called?
questions.explanation_correct: Development time is commonly measured from the beginning of first crack until the coffee is dropped from the roaster for cooling.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Drying occurs earlier, while cooling begins after the roast ends. Water quenching is optional, not required.

questions.question: What is the standard professional sensory evaluation protocol for assessing coffee quality in a controlled environment?
questions.explanation_correct: Cupping is an industry-standard method used by professionals to evaluate coffee quality via uniform tasting panels.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Grading is an assessment of physical defects, while tasting/scoring are general actions rather than specific set protocols.

questions.question: What fluid property describes resistance to flow and can affect how brewed coffee passes through a filter?
questions.explanation_correct: Viscosity describes resistance to flow. Pressure, bed permeability and particle distribution also affect the flow rate.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Density and surface tension are other fluid properties; boiling point is a phase-transition temperature.

questions.question: Which brown high-molecular-weight materials formed during roasting are associated with Maillard reactions and contribute to coffee color?
questions.explanation_correct: Melanoidins are brown high-molecular-weight materials formed mainly through Maillard-related reactions during roasting and contribute to coffee color and body.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Polyphenols, alkaloids and lipids are other classes of compounds, not the brown Maillard-derived material described.
